mainTopic: Why כותים may not marry into the Jewish people, and the משנה on checking a bride's female ancestors before marriage
overview: The amud opens by finishing the explanations of why חכמים barred כותים from marrying into the Jewish people. First reason: they read the יבום פסוק backwards, so married widows wed outsiders, and according to רבי עקיבא a child from such a לאו is a ממזר. Second reason, 'יש אומרים': כותים are not expert in the details of מצוות. רב אידי בר אבין shows that this is רבי אליעזר's view, and that here it means the laws of קידושין and גירושין. רב נחמן adds that ממזרים were mixed in among the כותים, and רבא says a slave and a maidservant were mixed in. Each time the גמרא asks why two examples are given, and answers that this is simply what happened. A new משנה then teaches which female ancestors a man must check before marrying a כהנת or another woman. It also teaches where the checking stops: at an ancestor who served at the מזבח, on the דוכן, in the סנהדרין, or in other trusted roles. The גמרא explains why only the mothers are checked, and why the woman need not check the man, citing רב. It then brings other counts of the mothers, twelve and sixteen, and starts comparing them. That comparison continues on the next amud.

steps.title: They exempt fully married widows from יבום
steps.stepSummary: The end of the reason already given: כותים exempt fully married widows from יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they exempt the women who were fully married.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the middle of a sentence. The reason given just before says that כותים do יבום with engaged widows but exempt fully married widows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly backwards from the real halacha. The real rule is that both an engaged widow and a married widow need יבום or חליצה. If a married widow is treated as free and marries someone else, she has married an outsider while still bound to her brother-in-law.

keyTerms.meaning: women who were fully married (after נישואין, not just engaged)
marriage of a childless widow to her late husband's brother

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think כותים skipped יבום altogether. They kept it, but applied it to the wrong women: engaged widows instead of married ones.

phrases.english: and they exempt the married women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reason the previous section gave for the כותים being barred.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותים exempt fully married widows from יבום, which is the reverse of the true halacha.

steps.title: How did they get this reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which reading of the פסוק led the כותים to this backwards practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did they learn from the פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the כותים were reading in the תורה that made them think this. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כותים accepted the written תורה, so their mistake must come from some reading of a פסוק. The גמרא wants to find the exact misreading.

keyTerms.meaning: what do they learn out (from the פסוק)?

phrases.english: What do they expound?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the practice described in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which reading of a פסוק led the כותים to do יבום with engaged widows and exempt married ones.

steps.title: Reading the word 'outside' as describing the widow
steps.stepSummary: The כותים read החוצה as describing the widow. A widow who 'sits outside' (only engaged) needs יבום. A widow who does not (fully married) may marry anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'The wife of the dead man shall not be outside, to a stranger.' They read it this way: the one who sits outside may not marry a stranger, but the one who does not sit outside may marry a stranger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the כותים' misreading of the פסוק about יבום. They took the word 'outside' as describing the widow herself instead of describing the man she marries.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real meaning is that she may not marry someone outside the family. The כותים joined 'outside' to the woman: an engaged woman still lives outside her husband's home, so she is the one bound to יבום. A married woman already lived in his home, so they thought she was free to marry an outsider.

keyTerms.meaning: the wife of the dead man
a stranger, a man outside the family

steps.confusionAlert: 'Sits outside' means she still lives outside her husband's house, because she was only engaged. It does not mean she is outside the family.

phrases.english: "The wife of the dead man shall not be
outside to a stranger"–
the one who sits outside,
phrases.notes: He means a woman who was only engaged, so she still lives outside her husband's home.

phrases.english: she shall not be married to a stranger,
but the one who does not sit outside –
may be married to a stranger.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תִהְיֶה אֵשֶׁת הַמֵּת הַחוּצָה לְאִישׁ זָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They read 'outside' as describing the widow. An engaged widow, who still sits outside, is bound to יבום. A married widow may marry a stranger.

steps.title: Why this makes them ממזרים: רבי עקיבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The mistake makes their children ממזרים, because רבי עקיבא holds that a child from a union forbidden by a לאו is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא follows his own view, since he says that a child from a union forbidden by a לאו is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why this mistake leads to a ban on marriage. According to רבי עקיבא, the children of these marriages are ממזרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow waiting for יבום who marries an outsider breaks only a לאו, not a sin punished by כרת. Most opinions say such a child is not a ממזר. רבי עקיבא, however, holds that even a לאו produces a ממזר, so the כותים' family lines are a real problem.

keyTerms.meaning: a child from a forbidden union, who may not marry into the community
unions forbidden by a negative commandment (a לאו)

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the יבום mistake to the actual reason for the ban. Without רבי עקיבא's wide view of ממזר, the mistake alone would not disqualify their children.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva follows his reasoning,
for he says: there is a mamzer
from those liable for negative prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows why the misreading of step 3 leads to a ban on marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, a child of a union forbidden by a לאו is a ממזר. So the children of a widow who married an outsider while bound to יבום are ממזרים.
steps.whatToRemember: First reason for the ban: כותים get יבום backwards, and according to רבי עקיבא the resulting children are ממזרים.

steps.title: A second reason: not expert in the details of מצוות
steps.stepSummary: An unnamed opinion, 'יש אומרים', gives a different reason: כותים are not careful experts in the fine details of מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: it is because they are not expert in the fine details of מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different reason for the ban on marrying כותים, given in the name of 'some say'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason is not about one specific wrong reading of a פסוק. It is a general worry that כותים are not careful with the details, so we cannot trust their halachic practice.

phrases.english: And some say:
because they are not well versed
in the details of מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין בְּדִקְדּוּקֵי מִצְוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reason for the same ban.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותים are barred because they are not expert in the details of מצוות.

steps.title: Who is 'some say'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the unnamed 'יש אומרים' is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is 'some say'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who stands behind the unnamed opinion. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming the תנא lets us see whether this view fits a known position he holds elsewhere.

phrases.english: Who is "some say"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who said the view in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא behind 'יש אומרים'.

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין: it is רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין says the 'יש אומרים' is רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said: it is רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי בר אבין names the opinion: it belongs to רבי אליעזר. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is pointing to another place where רבי אליעזר uses this same reason about כותים.

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said:
It is Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.

steps.title: Proof from the מצה of a כותי on פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the תנא קמא allows a כותי's מצה. רבי אליעזר forbids it because כותים are not expert in the details of מצוות. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says כותים are extra careful in any מצוה they took on.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: the מצה of a כותי is allowed, and a person fulfills his obligation with it on פסח. רבי אליעזר forbids it, because they are not expert in the details of מצוות. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: any מצוה that כותים took on, they are very careful with it, more than Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רב אידי בר אבין's claim. In a ברייתא about פסח, רבי אליעזר uses the exact same words, 'not expert in the details of מצוות'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the wording matches word for word, the 'יש אומרים' about marriage must be רבי אליעזר. The ברייתא also shows that others disagree: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל trusts כותים in a מצוה they took on, since they keep it very strictly.

keyTerms.meaning: that they took on and kept

phrases.english: As it is taught: the matza of a Samaritan is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: and a person fulfills his obligation with it on Passover,
but Rabbi Eliezer prohibits it,
because they are not well versed
in the details of מצוות.
phrases.notes: These are the exact words of 'יש אומרים' in step 5. That match is the whole proof.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
any מצוה that Samaritans have embraced –
they are very exacting in it,
more than Jews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim of step 7 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the מצה of a כותי, where רבי אליעזר gives the identical reason.

steps.title: What details are they not expert in here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: for marriage, which details are the כותים not expert in?
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, what does 'not expert' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which details the כותים get wrong when it comes to marriage. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מצה the worry is clear: the dough may have become חמץ. But how does lack of expertise affect whom one may marry? The גמרא wants to know which area of halacha is meant.

phrases.english: But here,
what are they not well versed in?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי אליעזר's general reason from step 8 and asks how it applies to marriage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which area of halacha the כותים are not expert in, such that it affects marrying them.

steps.title: Not expert in the laws of קידושין and גירושין
steps.stepSummary: The answer: כותים are not expert in the laws of קידושין and גירושין, so their marriages and divorces cannot be trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are not expert in the laws of קידושין and גירושין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the problem is the laws of קידושין and גירושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If their גט might not be valid, a woman they treat as divorced may still be married. Then her children from a new husband could be ממזרים. That is why one may not marry into their families.

keyTerms.meaning: betrothal, the first stage of marriage

steps.whatToRemember: Second reason for the ban (רבי אליעזר): כותים are not expert in the laws of קידושין and גירושין, so a woman may remarry with a bad divorce and her children may be ממזרים.

phrases.english: Because they are not well versed
in the laws of betrothal and divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין בְּתוֹרַת קִידּוּשִׁין וְגֵירוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The details meant are the laws of קידושין and גירושין.

steps.title: רב נחמן: ממזרים were mixed in among the כותים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, gives a different reason why the כותים cannot be married. Two kinds of ממזר became mixed in among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: A ממזר born from a man and his sister, and a ממזר born from a man and his brother's wife, were mixed in among the כותים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא gives his own reason why marrying a כותי is a problem. Some ממזרים got mixed into their population.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 blamed the problem on the כותים not knowing the laws of קידושין and גירושין. רב נחמן points to something else. Real ממזרים blended into the group, so nobody can tell who is a ממזר. That is why the whole group is treated as doubtful.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden relationship, who may not marry a regular Jew
Became mixed in, so you can no longer tell them apart
A brother's wife, a forbidden relationship

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
A mamzer born from his sister
and a mamzer born from a brother's wife
were mixed in among them.
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the כותים, the group we've been talking about.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reason for the lineage problem than the one in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כותים are of doubtful lineage because ממזרים from a sister and from a brother's wife were mixed in among them.

steps.title: Why mention two kinds of ממזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra detail teaches. If the point is that a child from a כרת relationship is a ממזר, one example would be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? That a child from a relationship punished by כרת is a ממזר? Then let him list just one example!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of רב נחמן's statement. Why did he name two kinds of ממזר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both cases, a sister and a brother's wife, are relationships punished by כרת. If he wanted to teach that a child from any כרת relationship is a ממזר, one case proves it. The second case looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Relationships punished by כרת (being cut off spiritually)

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
That there is a mamzer from those liable to karet?
Then let him teach one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's mention of two kinds of ממזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both examples teach the same rule, so naming both seems unnecessary.

steps.title: That is simply how it happened
steps.stepSummary: The answer: he was not teaching a new rule. He was describing the real event, and both kinds of ממזר really were mixed in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The incident that happened, happened that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two examples are not a lesson. They are simply what actually happened historically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed every detail must teach a law. The answer says this is a report of facts. Both kinds of ממזר really got mixed in, so both are mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: The event really happened this way

phrases.english: The incident that happened, happened this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical report, not a new rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two examples were meant to teach a law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The examples just describe what actually happened.

steps.title: רבא: a slave and a maidservant were mixed in
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives another reason. A Canaanite עבד and שפחה were mixed in among the כותים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A slave and a maidservant were mixed in among them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers yet another explanation of the lineage problem. Non-Jewish slaves got mixed into the כותים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not point to ממזרים. He points to people with slave status. A Jew may not marry someone of slave status, so once they blended in, the whole group became doubtful.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A slave and a maidservant were mixed in among them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another explanation, different from רב נחמן's in step 11 and from the earlier reasons in steps 4 and 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כותים are of doubtful lineage because an עבד and a שפחה were mixed in among them.

steps.title: Only the maidservant causes the problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the real problem comes only from the שפחה. So why mention the עבד too?
steps.simpleTranslation: The prohibition is because of what? Because of the maidservant! Then let him list just one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's wording. Only one of his two examples actually creates a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children of a שפחה are slaves, so her children cause the problem. The child of an עבד with a Jewish woman has fit lineage. So the עבד adds nothing, and naming him seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: The prohibition is because of what?
Because of the maidservant!
phrases.notes: Her children have slave status. The child of a slave with a Jewish woman does not.

phrases.english: Then let him teach one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of step 14, the same way step 12 challenged step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the שפחה causes a lineage problem, so mentioning the עבד seems pointless.

steps.title: Again, that is how it happened
steps.stepSummary: Same answer as before: both really were mixed in, so both are mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The incident that happened, happened this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as in step 13. The detail is a historical report, not a legal lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא was not claiming the עבד causes a problem. He was telling the story as it happened, and both a slave and a maidservant joined the group.
steps.whatToRemember: We now have four explanations for the כותים' problem. Steps 1-4 say they got יבום backwards, which makes ממזרים according to רבי עקיבא. Step 10 (יש אומרים, רבי אליעזר) says they were not expert in קידושין and גירושין. רב נחמן says ממזרים were mixed in among them, and רבא says a slave and a maidservant were mixed in. The extra details in the last two are just history: 'מעשה שהיה כך היה.'

phrases.english: The incident that happened, happened this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15, repeating the answer of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical report, not a new rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning the עבד implies he causes a lineage problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is mentioned only because he really was part of the event.

steps.title: New משנה: which mothers must be checked
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה starts. Before marrying a כהנת one checks four lines of mothers, eight women in total. For a לויה or ישראלית one adds one more generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who marries a woman who is a כהנת must check her background for four mothers, which are eight. He checks her mother and her mother's mother. He checks her mother's father's mother, and that woman's mother. He checks her father's mother, and that woman's mother. He checks her father's father's mother, and that woman's mother. For a לויה or ישראלית, one more is added.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists exactly which female ancestors must be checked for fit lineage before marrying a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four lines of grandmothers: her mother, her father's mother, her mother's father's mother, and her father's father's mother. For each one, you also check that woman's own mother, so 4 becomes 8. For a לויה or ישראלית, you go one generation further back. The משנה doesn't say why.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman from a כהן family
To check into her family background
A Levite woman and an Israelite woman

steps.confusionAlert: 'Four mothers which are eight' does not mean eight separate lines. It means four lines, and for each one you check her and her own mother.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who marries a woman who is a kohenet
must check into her background
for four mothers, which are eight:
her mother, and her mother's mother,
and the mother of her mother's father, and her mother,
phrases.notes: Each time 'and her mother' appears, it means the mother of the woman just named.

phrases.english: and her father's mother, and her mother,
and the mother of her father's father, and her mother.
A Levite woman and an Israelite woman
one adds onto them one more.
phrases.notes: One more generation back is checked.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנּוֹשֵׂא אִשָּׁה כֹּהֶנֶת צָרִיךְ לִבְדּוֹק אַחֲרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: checking lineage before marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before marrying a כהנת one checks eight female ancestors. For a לויה or ישראלית one adds one more generation.

steps.title: When checking can stop
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds where the checking ends. If an ancestor served at the מזבח, on the דוכן or in the סנהדרין, you stop there. Families whose ancestors were public officers or charity collectors need no checking at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: One does not check from the altar and above, nor from the platform and above, nor from the Sanhedrin and above. And anyone whose ancestors were known to be public officers or charity collectors may marry into the priesthood, and there is no need to check them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה limits the checking from the previous step. Certain positions prove an ancestor was already checked and found fit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן serving at the מזבח, a לוי singing on the דוכן, and a member of the סנהדרין all had their lineage examined before taking the role. So once you reach such an ancestor, there is no need to check further back. Families of public officers and charity collectors are trusted the same way, so they can marry into כהונה without any checking.

keyTerms.meaning: The altar in the בית המקדש, where כהנים served
The platform where the לויים sang in the בית המקדש
They may marry into the כהונה

steps.whatToRemember: Checking lineage goes back several generations, but it stops at any ancestor who held a role that required proven fit lineage.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בּוֹדְקִין לֹא מִן הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּלְמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: One does not check from the altar and above,
phrases.notes: 'And above' means going further back in the family tree past that ancestor.

phrases.english: nor from the platform and above,
nor from the Sanhedrin and above.
And anyone whose ancestors were known to be
among the public officers and charity collectors
may marry into the priesthood
and there is no need to check after them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בּוֹדְקִין לֹא מִן הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּלְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets limits on the checking required in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Checking stops at an ancestor who served at the מזבח, on the דוכן or in the סנהדרין. Families of public officers and charity collectors need no checking.

steps.title: Witnesses in the old court of ציפורי need no checking
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי adds to the משנה's list: a family whose ancestor signed as a witness in the old court of ציפורי does not need its lineage checked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Even someone who signed as a witness in the old court of ציפורי does not need checking.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps going with its list of families that need no checking. רבי יוסי adds one more kind of family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said that if an ancestor served as a public officer or charity collector, the family needs no checking. רבי יוסי says the same is true if an ancestor signed as a witness in the old court of ציפורי. Only people with clean lineage were allowed to sign there, so that signature already proves the family is fit.

keyTerms.meaning: A court (here, the old court of Tzippori)
Tzippori, a city in the Galil

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even one who had signed as a witness
in the old court of Tzippori
phrases.notes: He means this man's descendants also don't need their lineage checked, just like the families listed before.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אַף מִי שֶׁהָיָה חָתוּם עֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case to the משנה's list of families that need no checking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ancestor who signed as a witness in the old court of ציפורי frees the family from checking.

steps.title: Men in the king's army list need no checking
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס adds: a family whose ancestor was written in the Jewish king's army list does not need checking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס says: Even someone who was written in the king's army list does not need checking.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא adds one more family to the list of those that need no checking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only men of clean lineage were written into the king's army list. So being written there already proves the family is fit, and nobody needs to check further.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says:
Even one who was written
in the army list of the king

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends with a list of families that need no checking, because an ancestor held a role that only fit people could hold. These roles are the מזבח, the דוכן, the סנהדרין, public officer, charity collector, the old court of ציפורי and the king's army.
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר: אַף מִי שֶׁהָיָה מוּכְתָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another addition to the same list, and it closes the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ancestor listed in the king's army list frees the family from checking.

steps.title: Why check the mothers but not the fathers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה only checks the women in the bride's family and not the men.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is different about women, that we check them? And what is different about men, that we do not check them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. It asks why the check covers only the mothers' lines and not the fathers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 listed only mothers: four lines and eight women. A problem in lineage could just as easily come from a male ancestor, so the גמרא wants to know why the men are skipped.

phrases.english: Gemara
What is different about women, that we check them
and what is different about men, that we do not check them?
phrases.notes: He means the bride's male ancestors. The משנה only listed mothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא בִּנְשֵׁי בָּדְקִינַן וּמַאי שְׁנָא בְּגַבְרֵי דְּלָא בָּדְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first גמרא question on the משנה from Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the check is limited to the women in the family.

steps.title: Men's quarrels bring lineage problems into the open
steps.stepSummary: When women fight, they insult each other about immoral behavior, so a lineage problem stays hidden. When men fight, they insult each other about lineage, so any problem becomes known.
steps.simpleTranslation: When women quarrel, they quarrel about immoral behavior, so if there is a lineage problem, nobody hears about it. When men quarrel, they quarrel about lineage, so if there is a problem, it becomes known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. On the men's side, a lineage problem would already be public, so there is no need to check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking is only needed where a problem could stay hidden. In men's fights people shout out each other's family flaws, so any flaw on the father's side is already known. Women's fights are about other things, so a flaw on the mother's side might never come out, and it has to be checked.

phrases.english: Women, when they quarrel with each other,
it is about forbidden relations that they quarrel,
so if there is something wrong,
it does not become known.
Men, when they quarrel with each other,
it is about lineage that they quarrel,
so if there is something wrong,
it becomes known.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A flaw on the men's side becomes public through their quarrels, so only the women's side needs checking.

steps.title: Why doesn't the woman check the man?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why only the man checks the woman's family. The woman should also check the lineage of the man.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she too should check him himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty. The checking only goes one way, so it asks why the bride does not check the groom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts the duty to check only on the man marrying a כהנת or a fit woman. The גמרא asks why the woman doesn't have the same duty toward him.

phrases.english: And she too
should check him himself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new difficulty on the משנה, after the men-versus-women question was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that only the man checks the woman's lineage.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If lineage matters, both sides should have to check each other.

steps.title: Fit women may marry flawed men, as רב says
steps.stepSummary: The משנה supports רב, who says women of fit lineage were never forbidden to marry men of flawed lineage. So the woman has nothing to check.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב, as רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Women of fit lineage were not warned against marrying men of flawed lineage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing רב's rule. It also shows that the משנה supports him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lineage prohibitions are placed on the man, not the woman. A fit woman, such as a כהנת, is allowed to marry a man of flawed lineage, so she has no reason to check him. The fact that the משנה only makes the man check fits רב's view.

phrases.english: This supports Rav,
as Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Women of fit lineage were not warned
against marrying men of flawed lineage.

steps.whatToRemember: Only the man checks, because the lineage prohibitions fall on him. A fit woman is allowed to marry a man of flawed lineage, as רב says.
steps.triggerLanguage: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 23 and shows the משנה supports רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a known rule that removes the woman's need to check.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sides should check, since lineage matters to both.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fit women may marry flawed men, so the woman has nothing to check, and the משנה supports רב.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה counts twelve women
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה teaches that the four lines of mothers include twelve women, not the משנה's eight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה teaches: four mothers, which are twelve.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: how many women are counted in the four lines of mothers. רב אדא בר אהבה gives a count of twelve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in Step 17 said the four mothers come to eight women. רב אדא בר אהבה keeps the same four lines but counts more women in them, twelve in total.

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava teaches:
Four mothers, which are twelve.
phrases.notes: Our משנה said eight women. He counts more women within the same four lines.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה תָּנֵי: אַרְבַּע אִמָּהוֹת שֶׁהֵם שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה's count of eight women and gives a different count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four lines of mothers include twelve women.

steps.title: A ברייתא counts sixteen women
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the four lines of mothers include sixteen women.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a ברייתא it was taught: four mothers, which are sixteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third count, from a ברייתא: sixteen women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now three counts for the same four lines of mothers: eight in the משנה, twelve from רב אדא בר אהבה, and sixteen in the ברייתא. The גמרא will next try to explain how each count is reached.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: In a baraita it was taught:
Four mothers, which are sixteen.

steps.confusionAlert: All three counts speak of "four mothers." They do not disagree about the four lines. They only disagree about how many women are counted inside those lines: eight, twelve or sixteen.
steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: אַרְבַּע אִמָּהוֹת שֶׁהֵם שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another count, different from רב אדא בר אהבה's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four lines of mothers include sixteen women.

steps.title: Starting to explain the twelve count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins with "granted, according to רב אדא בר אהבה" to show his count is easy to understand. The difficulty with the other count comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to רב אדא בר אהבה,
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to explain why רב אדא בר אהבה's count makes sense before it questions the count of sixteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בשלמא ("granted") tells us one side is clear and the question will be on the other side. The sentence continues on the next amud, where the full question appears.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav Adda bar Ahava,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to compare the twelve and sixteen counts from Steps 25 and 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How each count is reached, starting with the one that is easy to understand.
